keep: The idea is named up front in plain words: one equation, term for term, mass as the coil, damper as the resistor, spring as 1 ÷ C.
Both equations are built from what Dan knows: Newton's second law for the spring, and the volts round a loop for the circuit, with v = L di/dt and i = q′.

The values are matched (1 kg and 1 H, 0.5 N·s/m and 0.5 Ω, 4 N/m and 1 ÷ 0.25 F), so one trace really is both, and every bar reading is computed from the rule (−2, 0, 2 at release; −0.78, −0.37, 1.15 at 0.5 s; 0.61, 0, −0.61 near 4.75 s).

Each misconception has a puzzle with a drawn wrong pick: still means no acceleration (screen 2), C instead of 1 ÷ C (screens 4, 11, 12), the time graph read as a path (screen 6), one starting value (screens 9 and 10), a sign lost when rearranging (screen 12).
The mass moves up and down beside its trace, level with its newest point, so the picture itself answers the graph-as-picture slip.
The worked example uses realistic parts (10 mH, 2 Ω, 100 µF, 12 V) in base units and ends on what the answer means in amps a second.
Every slider range keeps the motion swinging, so nothing here pre-empts the next lesson's three cases.
fix: Brief names two actions (let go, and move the marker). Make it one: moving the time marker along the curve.
Skipped causal step: the minus signs in m x″ = −k x − c x′ are not explained. Say the spring pulls back towards rest and the damper drags against the motion.
Skipped causal step: 'they add to zero at every moment' is asserted. Say why: the bars are the equation read at one moment.
False absolute risk: 'what you know of the circuit carries straight over to the spring' is too wide. Narrow it to any result for one giving the matching result for the other, in this model.
False absolute: 'a real coil with an iron core strays from it' holds only when the core is driven towards saturation. Say so.
Read-through: 'Lift the mass … and let go' and 'Charge the capacitor and close the loop' read as instructions in explain. Make them 'say the mass is lifted …'.
Unreadable labels: the slider range numbers have no unit in their labels. Add kg or H, N·s/m or Ω, N/m or per farad.
Practice worked example: '−1200 A a second' needs its meaning. Say the minus means the charge leaves the capacitor.
Explain runs to six paragraphs; fold the model note into the last and say the next lesson sorts the three kinds.
